title: Generation of Multicue Cellular Microenvironments by UV-Photopatterning of Three-Dimensional Cell Culture Substrates
protocol: Create a negative glass mold (#1) containing all features of interest using a femtosecond-laser direct-write technique.
Place the negative glass mold (#1) on the bottom of a Petri dish carefully.
Prepare PDMS prepolymer by placing an empty 50 mL conical tube on a scale, tare the scale, and pour the desired amount of silicone elastomer base into the tube.
Add curing agent using a Pasteur pipet so that the final ratio of elastomer base and curing agent is 10:1 (w/w).
Thoroughly mix the components in the conical tube using a spatula.
Centrifuge at 2,000 × g for 70 s to remove all air bubbles.
Pour the PDMS prepolymer on top of the negative glass mold (#1) in the Petri dish to cover it completely.
Place the Petri dish with the negative glass mold (#1) and the PDMS prepolymer in the vacuum desiccator.
Start the vacuum pump.
Wait for 5 min under vacuum to remove bubbles from the interface between the mold surface and the PDMS prepolymer.
Remove the vacuum and take the Petri dish out of the desiccator.
Cure the PDMS prepolymer overnight at 65 °C in the oven.
Carefully lift the edges of the newly cured positive PDMS chip (#2) from the negative glass mold (#1) using a spatula.
If the chip sticks to the mold, add ethanol or water to the edges while lifting.
Cut off the sides of the positive PDMS chip (#2) with a blade to create a rectangular shape.
Place the positive PDMS chip (#2) in a desiccator next to a vial containing tridecafluoro(1,1,2,2-tetrahydrooctyl)trichlorosilane and leave under vacuum overnight.
Place the positive PDMS chip in the bottom of a Petri dish.
Pour PDMS prepolymer on top of the positive PDMS chip to produce multiple negative PDMS molds.
Put the Petri dish under vacuum in the desiccator for 15 min to remove all bubbles.
Cure the PDMS prepolymer at 65 °C overnight.
Peel off the negative PDMS mold from the positive PDMS chip using a spatula.
Silanize the final negative PDMS mold using silanization agent in a vacuum desiccator overnight.
Pour PDMS prepolymer into the negative PDMS mold to produce multiple cell culture chips of approximately 5 mm thickness.
Remove bubbles from the poured PDMS prepolymer using the desiccator.
Cure the PDMS prepolymer for 3 h at 65 °C.
Cut the chip to the final size with a razor blade.
Prepare PDMS prepolymer according to steps 1.3-1.6.
Place a glass coverslip on the rounded vacuum post in the center of the spin coater.
Turn on the vacuum to attach the glass coverslip to the machine.
Pipette a droplet of PDMS in the middle of the coverslip using a Pasteur pipet.
Spincoat for 10 s at 0.45 × g, acceleration: 0.2 × g/s.
Spincoat for 50 s at 44.8 × g, acceleration: 0.54 × g/s.
Turn off the vacuum and remove the coverslip from the spin coater using tweezers.
Place the coverslip in a Petri dish.
Cure the PDMS overnight in the oven at 65 °C.
Store the cured PDMS at room temperature afterwards.
Activate the hydroxyl groups on the surface of the PDMS chip (#4) using O2-plasma.
Place the chip in the basket of the plasma asher using tweezers.
Run an ashing cycle using a power of 20 W for 30 s.
Vent the ashing chamber using N2.
Take the chip out of the basket and place it in a small PDMS container.
Add 500 μL of Poly-L-lysine (PLL, 0.01%) on top of the chip so that the complete surface is immersed in the PLL solution.
Incubate for 30 min at room temperature.
Remove 450 μL of the PLL using a pipet.
Rinse the chip surface three times with 500 μL of 0.1 M HEPES buffer (8 < pH < 8.5).
Make 500 μL of a 50 mg/mL methoxypolyethylene glycol-succinimidyl valerate (mPEG-SVA; MW 5,000 Da) solution in 0.1 M HEPES buffer (8 < pH < 8.5) per cell culture chip.
Incubate the mPEG-SVA on the sample for 60 min.
Remove 450 μL of the mPEG-SVA solution using a micropipet.
Wash the chip surface five times with phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Pipette up and down multiple times per wash to ensure all unbound mPEG-SVA is removed.
Store the samples by immersing them in PBS or continue to the patterning step of the protocol.
Store cured PDMS cell culture chips under dry conditions at room temperature.
Store passivated cell culture chips in PBS at 4°C for up to 7 days or store in dry conditions for up to several months.
To obtain dry samples, remove the PBS and rinse multiple times using double distilled water (ddH2O).
Blow-dry using a nitrogen- or air-gun.
Design digital masks using design software tools for patterning of 3D substrates.
Create a completely black artboard of 1,140 x 1,824 pixels.
Fill the artboard with the shapes of interest for patterning.
Export the artboard as an 8-bit TIFF-file.
Create a black artboard of the desired size in mm and fill the artboard with any shape of interest.
Divide the pattern into multiple files if needed for multi-focal plane patterning.
Save the artboard as a PDF-file.
Apply fluorescent highlighter on a glass coverslip.
Place the glass coverslip upside-down on the stage of the fluorescent microscope, ensuring the highlighted surface faces upwards.
Switch on the microscope and PRIMO equipment.
Open Micro-manager to access Leonardo software under 'plugins'.
Choose Calibration in the initial menu.
Select the 20x objective both on the microscope and in the software.
Click on Next.
Place the glass slide with fluorescent highlighter in the optical path of the microscope.
Switch to fluorescent mode.
Focus carefully on the PRIMO image, ensuring that both the logo and text are in focus.
Click on Next to finish the calibration procedure.
Write down the Z-location of the stage when calibrating.
Remove the calibration slide from the stage.
Place a glass slide containing a droplet (~50 µL) of photoinitiator (PLPP) in the stage.
Place the PDMS cell culture substrate upside-down in the droplet of photoinitiator.
Ensure that the 3D features on the surface of the cell culture substrate face the glass slide and are fully submerged in PLPP.
Select Pattern in the software.
Switch to brightfield mode on the microscope and move the stage to the feature of interest.
Focus on the top or bottom of convex and concave structures respectively.
Select PRIMO to insert a pattern of choice.
Adjust the patterning settings according to the feature (location, angle, repetitions).
Select a dose of 1,000 mJ/mm².
Click on Lock and switch the microscope to fluorescent mode.
Click on the Play button to start the patterning.
Once finished, observe the pattern displayed in green.
Remove the chip from the patterning slide after all features are completed.
Store the chip in PBS at 4°C.
Remove the calibration slide from the stage.
Place a glass slide containing a droplet (~50 µL) of photoinitiator (PLPP) in the stage.
Place the PDMS cell culture chip upside-down in the droplet of photoinitiator using tweezers.
Select Pattern in the software.
Switch to brightfield mode on the microscope.
Move the stage to the feature of interest.
Focus on the area of the chip at the right location.
Use multiple focal planes and multiple rounds of patterning per 3D substrate for sufficient pattern resolution along the complete height and width of the feature.
For a feature with a height of 150 µm, pattern in three rounds (± 1 focal plane per 50 µm of Z-travel), focusing around 25 µm, 75 µm, and 125 µm from the bottom of the feature.
Ensure that the bottom of the feature is at the value written down previously.
Select PRIMO to insert the pattern of choice.
Observe the pattern preview shown in orange on top of the live brightfield image.
Adjust the patterning settings according to the feature location and angle.
Select a dose of 1,000 mJ/mm².
Click on Lock and switch the microscope to fluorescent mode.
Click on the Play button to start the patterning.
Observe the pattern displayed in green.
Repeat steps for multiple focal planes as needed.
Remove the chip from the patterning slide after completion.
Store the chip in PBS at 4 °C.
Transfer the patterned cell culture chip to sterile PDMS containers if not already done under sterile conditions.
Wash the patterned cell culture chips three times with an excess of sterile PBS if necessary.
Prepare a fresh protein solution in PBS.
Add 2 mL of PBS using a micropipette to a vial of 20 µg of rhodamine-labeled fibronectin to obtain a concentration of 10 µg/mL.
Pipet gently to avoid the formation of protein clumps and protect from light.
Thaw a 200 µL aliquot of dissolved gelatin-fluorescein.
Protect from light.
Add 200-500 µL of the protein solution to the cell culture chip using a micropipette.
Incubate fibronectin for 5 min at room temperature.
Incubate gelatin for 15 min at 37 °C.
Cover the sample with aluminum foil during incubation.
Remove the protein solution and wash 5x with 500 µL of sterile PBS.
Pipet the PBS up and down multiple times above all relevant features of the cell culture chip to remove any unbound protein.
Keep the samples sterile and immersed in PBS.
Detach cells of interest using trypsin.
Prepare a cell suspension of 1 mL containing approximately 10,000-50,000 cells/mL in culture medium per chip.
Remove PBS from the cell culture chip and add 1 mL of the prepared cell suspension.
Incubate the cell culture chip with cells for 60 min at 37 °C.
Check the adhesion of cells on the patterned cell culture chip under a brightfield microscope.
Look for elongated cell morphologies in line patterns.
Remove medium up and down above cells adhering outside the patterned area to detach them.
Place the cell culture chip in a 6-well plate filled with ~5 mL of culture medium.
Culture cells for the desired length of time.
Replace the cell culture medium every 2-3 days.
After the desired length of culture, remove almost all the medium and wash three times with excess PBS.
Incubate with 3.7% formalin for 15 min at room temperature.
Wash three times with PBS for 5 min per wash at room temperature.
Never let the sample dry out during fixation and staining.
Stain the cell culture substrate with the desired staining agents or antibodies.
Place the cell culture chips upside-down in a droplet of staining solution pipeted on a glass slide.
Store the samples in PBS (short-term) or attached to a coverslip using mounting medium (long-term) at 4 °C.
Place the stained sample upside down in a droplet of PBS on a glass slide.
Put the sample in the stage of a confocal microscope.
Make Z-stacks with a suitable objective and Z-spacing to ensure proper image acquisition.
Open the raw image files in image analysis software.
Check that the image properties (e.g., dimensions, resolution) are correct.
Adjust the brightness and contrast per channel if needed.
Crop the region of interest containing the pattern and cells.
Perform a deconvolution step if needed.
Create a 3D render of the Z-stack using 3D rendering software.
Optimize the contrast and gain settings for each individual channel.
Create a snapshot of the 3D render and export as .TIFF file.
Set the start and final frame as well as the timeframe before registering the movie.
Export the movie of the 3D render as .avi.
